## What this does

Plumbing, not part of the method itself. `Arr2` is a plain 2-D table (rows
× columns), standing in for the original Fortran's statically-sized 2-D
arrays — e.g. one row per site, one column per species, holding whether
that species was recorded there (`idata`), whether it counts as a
benchmark species there (`ibench`), or its pooled local frequency
(`ffij`). `new` allocates a table of a given size, pre-filled with a
starting value; `at` reads one cell.

### `Arr2::new`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Arr2__new"}
    pub fn new(nrows: usize, ncols: usize, init: T) -> Self {
        Arr2 {
            data: vec![init; (nrows + 1) * (ncols + 1)],
            stride: ncols + 1,
        }
    }
```

### `Arr2::at`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Arr2__at"}
    pub fn at(&self, i: usize, j: usize) -> T {
        self.data[i * self.stride + j]
    }
```
